recoveryMode.title: Recovery mode
recoveryMode.subtitle: Whether this deployment is running in recovery mode, and how to enter or exit it.
recoveryMode.status_active_help: This deployment is running in recovery mode. Unauthorized kryphocron.* writes are being bypassed so corrupted state can be repaired.
recoveryMode.status_inactive_help: This deployment is running normally. Recovery-mode write bypass is not in effect.
recoveryMode.about_body: Recovery mode is a corruption-recovery fail-safe. While active, it relaxes one specific guard so an operator can repair state that normal authorization would block:
recoveryMode.effect_bypass: Unauthorized tools.kryphocron.* writes are routed through with a synthesized RecoveryBypass authorization (lexicon validation, closed-namespace deny, and the dedicated-endpoint requirement are skipped for that branch only).
recoveryMode.effect_audited: Every recovery write lands a kryphocron_recovery_write moderation event in the audit chain, queryable via moderator.queryEvents — recovery is bypass-with-a-trail, never silent.
recoveryMode.effect_preserved: Recovery mode does NOT override the kryphocron master switch, authentication, takedowns, or any deny upstream of that branch.
recoveryMode.procedure_intro: Recovery mode is entered at process start and exited by restart — deliberately, so it can't be toggled at runtime. There is no enter/exit button by design.
recoveryMode.enter_body: Restart the deployment with the environment variable set, then confirm the state above shows Active:
recoveryMode.exit_body: Restart the deployment without AURORA_RECOVERY_MODE set (or set to anything other than 'true' / '1'). The state above returns to Inactive.
recoveryMode.no_runtime_note: There is intentionally no runtime control to enter or exit recovery mode: a corruption-recovery bypass that could be flipped on via the admin API would be a security liability, so it is bound to process startup.

rebuild.title: Repository rebuild
rebuild.subtitle: Reconstruct a single account's repository from its sequencer history, then atomically swap it in. A recovery operation, not a routine action.
rebuild.did_help: The account whose repository to rebuild.
rebuild.deep_help: Reconstructs and cryptographically verifies the repository before any change. Slower — it reads and decodes every commit.
rebuild.check_intro: What a rebuild would reconstruct from the sequencer.
rebuild.check_empty: Run a pre-rebuild check to see what would be reconstructed.
rebuild.deep_blocked: Rebuild is blocked until verification passes. Diagnostic: {message}
rebuild.history_verify_ok: Verifies across full history ({commits} commits, {keys} keys)
rebuild.history_verify_blocked: History-aware verification failed — a commit in this account's history does not verify against the signing key valid at its revision. Rebuild is blocked pending investigation.
rebuild.no_history: No sequencer history for this account — nothing to rebuild.
rebuild.action_intro: Reconstructs the repository in memory and atomically swaps it in. The original is untouched unless the swap succeeds.
rebuild.confirm_body: This reconstructs {did} from {commits} sequencer commits and atomically replaces its live repository. The cost scales with history length. Type REBUILD to confirm.
rebuild.in_flight: A rebuild is already in flight for this account.
rebuild.cancel_pending: Cancellation requested — the rebuild will stop at the next safe point.
rebuild.cancel_note: Cancelling is clean during walking and verifying; the final swap is atomic and cannot be interrupted.
rebuild.cancel_confirm_body: The rebuild will stop and the original repository will be left untouched.
rebuild.cancel_none: This rebuild has already finished — nothing to cancel.
rebuild.cancelled_summary: Rebuild cancelled before the swap — the original repository is untouched.
rebuild.invalid_did: Enter a valid DID (did:plc:… or did:web:…).

repair.title: Repository repair
repair.subtitle: Scan every account for repo-vs-sequencer inconsistencies, then bulk-repair all or a selected subset. Each repair is a per-account rebuild.
repair.scan_explainer: Walks every account and structurally reconstructs its repository from the sequencer, recording any account whose live repo diverges. Read-only — it detects, it does not repair.
repair.scan_in_progress: A scan is already in progress.
repair.scan_cancel_pending: Cancellation requested — the scan will stop at the next account.
repair.findings_empty: No inconsistencies found. Run a scan to refresh.
repair.repair_explainer: Repairs reconstruct each account's repository and atomically swap it in — the same operation as a single repository rebuild, run across the selected accounts. A per-account failure is skipped, not fatal to the batch.
repair.confirm_body_all: This rebuilds every account in the current findings, atomically replacing each live repository. Type REPAIR to confirm.
repair.confirm_body_selected: This rebuilds {count} selected account(s), atomically replacing each live repository. Type REPAIR to confirm.
repair.repair_in_progress: A bulk repair is already in progress.
repair.repair_cancel_pending: Cancellation requested — the batch will stop before the next account.
repair.repair_cancel_note: Cancelling stops before the next account; an account already mid-rebuild finishes (its swap is atomic).
repair.repair_cancel_none: This bulk repair has already finished — nothing to cancel.

seqRecovery.title: Sequencer recovery
seqRecovery.subtitle: Escalation surface for sequencer-level intervention beyond the routine pause/resume/reset controls. v0.9 offers a read-only deep integrity validation.
seqRecovery.op_explainer: Walks the live sequencer log, decoding every event and checking per-DID revision monotonicity. Finds undecodable event blobs (which the firehose silently drops) and concurrent-write ordering anomalies. Read-only — it reports, it does not modify the sequencer.
seqRecovery.run_in_progress: A sequencer recovery operation is already in progress.
seqRecovery.cancel_pending: Cancellation requested — the validation will stop at the next page.
seqRecovery.cancel_none: No validation is in progress — nothing to cancel.
seqRecovery.report_clean: No anomalies found — the live sequencer log decodes cleanly and is per-DID monotonic.
seqRecovery.affected_help: {count} account(s) have at least one malformed event. Each can be repaired by rebuilding its repository from history (§7.4.1). Open any account to rebuild it individually, or route all of them below.
seqRecovery.route_confirm_body: This queues a repository rebuild for {count} affected account(s), re-deriving each repo from its sequencer history. Each rebuild is destructive (atomic swap) and audited. Accounts with a rebuild already in flight are skipped.
seqRecovery.route_started: Routing complete: {queued} rebuild(s) queued, {skipped} skipped (already in flight).
seqRecovery.route_unavailable: Nothing to route — run a deep validation that finds malformed events first.

laquna.title: Laquna
laquna.subtitle: Deployment-wide Laquna rotation. The one-button surface.
laquna.rotate_explainer: Rotating re-encodes existing kryphocron private-tier records under a new generation. CIDs change; at-URIs stay stable, so external references remain valid. A full rewrite takes time proportional to record volume.
laquna.rotate_not: This is friction-as-filtering against casual harvest — not encryption, and not security against a motivated adversary.
laquna.rotate_confirm_body: This rotates the slug and re-encodes every private-tier record under the new generation. Type ROTATE to confirm. Recorded in the audit chain.
laquna.rotate_in_progress: A rotation is already in progress.
laquna.cancel_pending: Cancellation requested — the job will stop at its next batch boundary.
laquna.cancel_confirm_body: Stop the in-progress rewrite at its next batch boundary? A partial rewrite is safe — records carry their own generation and decode regardless. You can re-trigger later.
laquna.cancel_none: No rotation is in progress to cancel.
laquna.cadence_help: Deployment cadence for organic slug rotation, plus the per-account override range. SuperAdmin-write.
laquna.cadence_save_body: Save the rotation cadence and per-account range? Recorded in the audit chain.
